overview: CG Oncology (CGON) is a Dallas, Texas-based late-stage biotech focused on bladder cancer. Founded in 2010 as Cold Genesys, it is developing a single product candidate across multiple non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) settings.

Cretostimogene grenadenorepvec is an oncolytic immunotherapy delivered directly into the bladder. It is designed to replicate in and kill tumor cells while stimulating an anti-tumor immune response. Results from the pivotal BOND-003 trial in high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ were published in The Lancet Oncology in July 2026, and the company expects to complete its BLA in Q4 2026.

The second Phase 3, PIVOT-006, tests cretostimogene as adjuvant therapy in intermediate-risk NMIBC — a larger population — and has accrued the vast majority of target events with topline data expected near term. CORE-008, a multi-cohort Phase 2, extends into BCG-exposed and BCG-naïve high-risk disease.

Investor thesis: CGON is a pure-play bet on becoming a bladder-sparing standard of care in NMIBC. With ~$1B in cash and runway through 2029, it can fund the launch independently. The key questions are whether PIVOT-006 expands the label into intermediate-risk disease and how cretostimogene competes with J&J's TAR-200 and ImmunityBio's Anktiva.

competitors.name: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ)
competitors.note: Big pharma intravesical competitor in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC

competitors.name: ImmunityBio (IBRX)
competitors.note: Approved IL-15 agonist in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS

advantage: Strong complete-response data with a favorable tolerability profile, a second Phase 3 targeting the larger intermediate-risk population, and one of the strongest balance sheets among small/mid-cap oncology biotechs.

catalysts.title: PIVOT-006 Phase 3 Topline Data
catalysts.description: Adjuvant therapy in intermediate-risk NMIBC; positive data would substantially expand the addressable market.

catalysts.title: BLA Completion
catalysts.description: Completion of the BLA for high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC.

catalysts.title: CORE-008 Durability Data
catalysts.description: Durability data across high-risk BCG-exposed and BCG-naïve cohorts.

catalysts.title: FDA Approval Decision
catalysts.description: Timing depends on BLA acceptance and review designation.

risks.title: Single-Asset Company
risks.description: The entire valuation rests on cretostimogene; a setback in PIVOT-006 or the BLA would hit hard.

risks.title: Competitive Market
risks.description: J&J, ImmunityBio and Ferring already have or are nearing approved options in the same setting.

risks.title: Manufacturing
risks.description: Viral immunotherapy manufacturing (CMC) is complex; CMC costs are already driving higher R&D spend.

risks.title: Valuation
risks.description: At ~$6.4B market cap, much of the approval scenario appears priced in.

risks.title: Commercial Build-Out
risks.description: Rising G&A ($29.0M in Q2 2026) reflects a first-time launch build that must reach urologists effectively.

partners.name: Expanded Access Program
partners.description: Provides cretostimogene to eligible patients outside trials ahead of approval.

partners.name: Clinical Trial Network
partners.description: BOND-003, PIVOT-006 and CORE-008 are run across U.S. and international urology centers.

interpretation: ~$1.0B in cash with management guidance through 2029 means CGON can fund a U.S. launch without needing to raise capital, removing a common overhang for single-asset biotechs.
